question: My employer 401k match is only 1%. Should I still max it out before contributing elsewhere?
plausible_answers: Answer A (Match Then IRA Default): Contribute just enough to get the 1% match, then direct all remaining retirement savings to a Roth or traditional IRA — better investment options and lower fees in the IRA outweigh the minimal 401k match beyond the free money.
Answer B (Max 401k First): Max the 401k entirely before the IRA if you're a high earner seeking maximum pre-tax deductions — the tax benefit outweighs the fee disadvantage at high income levels.

Answer C (IRA Only After Match): After capturing the match, skip the 401k entirely until the IRA is maxed — the investment flexibility and lower costs of a self-directed IRA deliver better long-term outcomes for most investors.
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Fidelity, USA): Even a 1% match is a 100% instant return on that portion — always contribute at least enough to capture the full match before directing money elsewhere, regardless of match size.

Source 2 (2022, NerdWallet, USA): After capturing the employer match, most advisors recommend prioritizing a Roth or traditional IRA next due to broader investment options and potentially lower fees than typical 401k plans.

Source 3 (2023, Investopedia, USA): Many 401k plans have limited investment options and higher expense ratios than IRAs; once the match is captured, an IRA often provides better net returns through lower-cost index funds.

Source 4 (2022, Reddit r/personalfinance, USA): Community standard order: 401k to match → Roth IRA to max → back to 401k to max → taxable brokerage. With only a 1% match the 401k quickly becomes lower priority after the IRA is maxed.

Source 5 (2021, Morningstar, USA): For high earners above Roth income limits, maxing the 401k before or alongside an IRA becomes more attractive due to the pre-tax deduction and backdoor Roth conversion opportunities.
